value.body: An airport customer service agent handles passengers on the ground for an airline or a ground-handling company: check-in, baggage, boarding, and help during delays or cancellations. The work is at airport counters and gates, in shifts that follow the flight schedule.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: Class 12 pass or a degree, plus an airport entry pass

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Airline departure control and reservation systems

items.label: Air passengers at Indian airports
items.note: Domestic and international passengers handled across Indian airports
items.source: Airport traffic for FY 2023-24, ICRA (as reported)

items.label: Operational airports
items.note: Count given by the AAI Chairman in October 2025

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Airlines and ground-handling companies recruit through walk-ins and online applications; selection is usually an interview with a communication assessment. New hires are trained on the airline's systems and need a security background check for an airport entry pass.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Clear communication in English and a local language

value.title: At a glance
items: Shift work includes early mornings, nights and holidays.
Next roles: senior agent, duty officer, or station operations roles.
Some move from here into cabin crew or hospitality jobs.
